tagline: Up the Skykomish behind the railroad, and down into Bavaria.
intro: US 2 leaves Monroe up the Skykomish valley through Sultan and Gold Bar. At Index it takes the South Fork into the mountains, past Skykomish, a railroad town with no road out but this one, and climbs to Stevens Pass at 4,061 feet, where the Pacific Crest Trail crosses. The east side comes down the Wenatchee valley to Leavenworth and Peshastin.

The road keeps company with the Great Northern, finished in 1893. John Stevens, who surveyed the pass for it in 1890, found no trail, no blaze and no old campfire for ten miles either way. The trains now run through a tunnel 1,180 feet under the summit.

moments.title: Wallace Falls
moments.text: A mile out of Gold Bar, trails climb past the ruins of logging trestles to a 367-foot fall whose longest drop shows from the Skykomish Valley.

moments.title: Index
moments.text: The smallest town in the county, 155 people, named for a peak shaped like an index finger. Climbers come for the cliffs of the Index Town Wall.

moments.title: Leavenworth
moments.text: A struggling logging town that in the 1960s made its whole center over as a Bavarian village, beginning with a fire-damaged hotel reopened as the Edelweiss in 1965.

practical: The pass is usually open all year but can close for a time in heavy winter snow. Check WSDOT mountain pass conditions before a winter crossing.
